article.title: Regression to the Mean: Why Your Best Customers Often Look Worse Next Year
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: Businesses often select their best customers by looking at the highest spenders in one period. When the same customers are examined next year, their average spending frequently falls. It is tempting to conclude that loyalty weakened or that the company failed to retain value. Part of the decline, however, may be regression to the mean. Observed performance contains both a persistent component and temporary variation. A customer may have unusually high spending this year because of a large one-time purchase, a household event, a promotion, or simple random fluctuation. If customers are selected precisely because their observed value was extreme, the selected group contains many cases that benefited from positive temporary variation. In the next period, that temporary boost is unlikely to repeat for everyone, so the group average naturally moves closer to its long-run level. This does not mean behavior never changes. It means that a before-and-after decline among an extreme group is not sufficient evidence of deterioration. The same logic applies to low-performing groups, which may improve next year even without an intervention. Regression to the mean is especially relevant to decile analysis, VIP programs, risk flags, and campaigns that target customers after an unusually strong or weak period. Analysts can reduce misinterpretation in several ways. One is to use multiple historical periods when defining stable high-value customers instead of selecting on a single noisy period. Another is to compare the selected group with an appropriate control or reference group exposed to the same calendar conditions. A randomized experiment is stronger when evaluating an intervention because both treatment and control groups are subject to regression to the mean. Analysts can also model expected future value using shrinkage or hierarchical approaches that distinguish persistent differences from noise. The reporting language should reflect the design. “Customers in last year’s top decile spent less this year” is an observation. “Top customers are becoming less loyal” is a causal or behavioral interpretation that requires more evidence. It is also important to distinguish migration caused by relative ranking from absolute spending changes. A customer can move from decile one to decile two even when spending rises if other customers rise faster. Conversely, a customer may remain in the top decile while spending falls if the entire distribution declines. Regression to the mean reminds analysts that selecting extreme observations changes what should be expected next. When a group is chosen because it was exceptional, some movement toward normal is mathematically ordinary, not automatically a business failure. Analysts should document the population, observation window, assumptions, and operational definition before drawing a conclusion. A useful review separates the observed metric from the mechanism that may have produced it and from the action that should follow. This discipline makes the result easier to reproduce, challenge, and communicate to stakeholders. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本文的核心不是只看表面指標，而是先確認母體、分母、時間範圍與選擇機制，再判斷數字是否真的代表 business outcome 改善。分析時要區分觀察事實、可能機制與因果結論，並把不確定性、經濟價值與下一步 action 一起納入。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：表面的なmetricだけで結論を出さず、母集団、分母、期間、selection mechanismを確認したうえでbusiness outcomeの改善を判断する。観察事実、考えられるmechanism、因果的な結論を分け、不確実性、経済価値、次のactionまで含めて説明することが重要である。
